assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optical lattice clocks, trapping atoms at the magic wavelength where the lattice light shift cancels, opened a route to fractional frequency uncertainties near 1e-18 and have redefined what precision timekeeping, relativistic geodesy and tests of fundamental constants can do. The idea is original and conceptually clean, and the impact is already broad across metrology, AMO physics and searches for new physics.
assessment.attribution: Katori proposed the magic-wavelength lattice concept and demonstrated the first lattice clock; Jun Ye's group drove the strontium clock to the lowest uncertainties and the many-body and applications side. Two laureates give a coherent and defensible configuration. Other contributors, for example in ion clocks and the frequency-comb link, are outside this candidate's credited names and would sit in related recognition.
assessment.maturity: Independently confirmed by several laboratories worldwide with multiple atomic species, stable interpretation and steady improvement for two decades. Timing is good; a redefinition of the second is under discussion but not required for the physics to be mature.
uncertainties: Overlap with the earlier 2005 and 2012 prizes on frequency combs and trapped-ion control may influence how the committee frames novelty.
Whether the prize should name a third contributor from related lattice-clock work is not settled by the supplied credit.
I am an atomic theorist and may be biased toward AMO precision topics; I have no stated personal connection to these two individuals beyond the field.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Magic-angle twisted bilayer graphene opened a new platform in which flat bands, correlated insulators and unconventional superconductivity can be tuned electrically, spawning the whole field of moire quantum matter. The theoretical prediction of the magic angle followed by quick experimental realisation is an unusually clear case of discovery with large downstream impact.
assessment.attribution: Bistritzer and MacDonald made the continuum-model prediction of flat bands at a magic angle; Jarillo-Herrero's group made the decisive experimental discovery of correlated insulating states and superconductivity. The three-person split between prediction and experiment is natural. Pablo Jarillo-Herrero's collaborators on the 2018 papers, notably Yuan Cao, are not in the credited list and the question of junior credit is open.
assessment.maturity: Strong reproduction across many groups since 2018, with extension to other moire systems; the microscopic origin of superconductivity remains debated, but the existence and tunability of the phenomena are firmly established. Timing is arguably early but not unreasonable.
uncertainties: Pairing mechanism of the superconducting state is unresolved.
Role of other early theorists of twisted bilayers and of Cao and collaborators is not covered by the credited names.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ultracold atoms in optical lattices realise the Hubbard model with tunable parameters, giving the Mott insulator transition, single-site-resolved quantum gas microscopy and a general platform for quantum many-body simulation. Originality and clarity are high and the impact spans AMO, condensed-matter and quantum-information physics.
assessment.attribution: The Jaksch-Zoller proposal supplied the theory, Greiner and Bloch the Mott transition and later microscopy. The credited list has four names and I would limit the prize to three; I choose the two leading experimenters and one theorist. Cirac, whose theory work is also central, is left out only because of the three-person limit, and that choice is a real allocation dilemma that overlaps with B031.
assessment.maturity: Mott transition observed in 2002 and broad confirmation since, with quantum gas microscopes in many laboratories; the field is mature and the techniques are stable. Recognition is timely; progress towards a useful simulation advantage continues.
uncertainties: Choosing between Zoller and Cirac, and between Greiner and other microscopy pioneers, is contentious.
Ultracold atoms already received the 1997 and 2001 prizes, so the committee may prefer a narrower citation.
Whether quantum simulation has delivered new physics beyond known models may be questioned.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: IceCube's discovery of a diffuse flux of astrophysical neutrinos at TeV-PeV energies, and the identification of the blazar TXS 0506+056 and the Galactic plane as sources, established neutrino astronomy as a new window on the high-energy universe. It is a large instrumental achievement with a clear discovery outcome.
assessment.attribution: Halzen conceived and led the cubic-kilometre Antarctic ice detector concept; Karle was a central figure on the detector and the analysis. In such a very large collaboration, the credited trio is imperfect, and I prefer two names; Yoshida's contribution is real but I judge it less decisive on the supplied evidence. Credit to the wider collaboration and to earlier pioneers such as the AMANDA and DUMAND efforts is a structural problem.
assessment.maturity: The diffuse flux is robust at many sigma and the source identifications are at the 3-5 sigma level with additional data accumulating. Complementary experiments such as KM3NeT are still developing; the field is maturing and the prize would be reasonable but the physics interpretation is still evolving.
uncertainties: Source-level evidence is statistically moderate for some claims.
A prize for a large collaboration has attribution difficulties and the previous 2002 prize for neutrino astronomy overlaps.
My knowledge of the internal leadership roles is not independently verified.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The quantum spin Hall effect and topological insulators created a distinct class of materials with protected edge and surface states governed by time-reversal symmetry and the Z2 invariant. This is a conceptually deep advance extending the topological-phase Nobel prize of 2016, with wide experimental and theoretical consequences.
assessment.attribution: Kane and Mele made the theoretical prediction and introduced the Z2 classification; Molenkamp's group gave the first experimental observation of the quantum spin Hall effect in HgTe wells after the Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang proposal. Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang and the 3D topological insulator work of Hasan, Moore, Balents and others are not all covered, so the allocation is contested.
assessment.maturity: Many independent confirmations, including ARPES and transport measurements, and a mature theoretical framework. Recognition is timely and arguably overdue relative to confirmation.
uncertainties: Credit for the HgTe proposal and for three-dimensional topological insulators is contested among several groups.
Potential overlap with B009 and the quantum anomalous Hall candidates would need coordinated treatment.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Anyons, quasiparticles in two dimensions with fractional exchange statistics, are a fundamental extension of the boson-fermion dichotomy; their relevance to topological quantum computation adds weight. The conceptual originality is high.
assessment.attribution: Leinaas and Myrheim made the foundational 1977 theoretical prediction of intermediate statistics in low dimensions. On the experimental side the credited names include Heiblum, Manfra and Fève and Rosenow; I select Fève for the Hanbury Brown-Twiss collider demonstration of fractional statistics, but Heiblum's and Manfra's interferometer experiments are comparable, so which experimentalist should be recognised is unresolved. Wilczek and Halperin, who gave key theoretical contributions, are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Experimental evidence emerged in 2020 through two independent approaches, with further work since, so independent confirmation exists but is recent, and interpretation of interferometer data has met alternative explanations. Likely premature compared with other candidates.
uncertainties: Missing theoretical credit for Wilczek and Halperin, and Arovas, Schrieffer and Wilczek.
Experimental attribution among Fève, Heiblum and Manfra is unsettled.
Non-Abelian anyons have not been demonstrated conclusively.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Circuit quantum electrodynamics established strong coupling of superconducting qubits to microwave resonators, enabling dispersive readout, control and the architecture for superconducting quantum processors. The clarity and impact are high, and the recognition of macroscopic quantum circuits in 2025 may make the field timely or alternatively already covered.
assessment.attribution: Blais and colleagues provided the 2004 theory proposal, Wallraff and Schoelkopf the 2004 experimental demonstration. Girvin's role in the Yale theory is also major, so the cut to three is a real compromise. The proposal-demonstration pairing is attractive for a prize.
assessment.maturity: Reproduced extensively and underpinning technology across the world; interpretation is stable. A strong maturity profile, though the 2025 prize narrows the sensible room for another superconducting-circuit award soon after.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2025 prize for macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits.
Omission of Girvin and the role of the Yale and Saclay groups in building the field is an unresolved credit issue.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Atom interferometry uses matter-wave interference for precise measurements of gravity, rotation and fundamental constants, and now supports tests of the equivalence principle and gravitational-wave detector concepts. It is a mature and original use of laser cooling and coherent atom optics, with a lasting measurement impact.
assessment.attribution: Pritchard pioneered the early atom interferometer with nanofabricated gratings and Kasevich and Chu demonstrated the light-pulse atom interferometer, with high-precision gravimetry and gradiometry; Chu is not in the credited list and Borde's role in the Ramsey-Borde scheme is real. I choose Kasevich and Pritchard but the allocation is contested, including with respect to earlier recognition of laser cooling.
assessment.maturity: Confirmed by many groups, with commercial and field-deployed instruments, though the strongest fundamental-physics payoffs such as detecting gravitational waves remain prospective. Timing is acceptable rather than urgent.
uncertainties: Steven Chu's absence from the credited names and previous 1997 laser cooling prize complicate the narrative.
Ranking is partly an acknowledgement of my own AMO domain familiarity, not an independent verification.
